picks.title: Design together with code layers on the canvas
picks.excerpt: Code layers is now in open beta. Teams can build code-backed prototypes on the Figma canvas, starting from GitHub, a local folder, a prototype brought in through the Figma MCP server, or a live site captured with the Chrome extension, and then compare variations side by side.
picks.rationale: Open-beta release that puts code-backed prototypes directly on the Figma canvas, which changes how designers prototype starting tomorrow.

picks.title: Introducing Krea 3
picks.excerpt: Krea released Krea 3, a new image editing model. Most edits finish in under 8 seconds at native 2K for $0.06 an image, take up to 6 reference images, and keep products and characters consistent from one image to the next. It is live for Krea's 30M users and through fal, Replicate and OpenRouter.
picks.rationale: New image-editing model with concrete speed, price and consistency numbers, already available through Krea and the major APIs.

picks.title: Cloud Agent Canvases and Environment Improvements
picks.excerpt: Cursor's cloud agents can now build interactive canvases as part of their work and share them with a team by link. An Environments API also entered beta, with support for up to 300 repos per environment.
picks.rationale: Shipped changelog feature: agents produce shareable interactive canvases, a new review surface for design-engineering teams.

picks.title: Vercel Ship 2026 recap
picks.excerpt: Vercel's Ship recap includes SAP rebuilding its design system to be composable so that people and agents assemble interfaces from the same parts with v0 and json-render, ZoomInfo embedding v0 for 40,000+ customers, and Notion's Ivan Zhao telling designers to 'design the API first and the UI last'.
picks.rationale: Concrete design-system case (SAP rebuilt for agent assembly via v0 and json-render) from a fresh event, not yet covered.

picks.title: Human in the loop means making sure the human is not out of the loop
picks.excerpt: Agents now act before we ask and reach past what we authorized. Patrick Neeman argues that a person in the loop is not enough if nobody owns the outcome, and lists what designers should consider when designing agent experiences.
picks.rationale: Practical checklist for designing agent experiences around outcome ownership; the strongest of the essay pool and fills the workflow slot.
